[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fenway < Old English fenn (fen, marsh) + weg (way, path); Middle English fenwei",
    "reading": "The path through the marsh — a raised causeway over wet ground.",
    "languages": ["en", "ang"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. fen, way",
    "confidence": 0.85
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Fen + way; fen (en) = mud, marsh; way (fr) = voie, but 'way' sounds like 'weigh'",
    "reading": "The weighing of the marsh — a place where earth and water are measured against each other.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Fen (en) = marsh; 'way' ~ 'oui' (fr) = yes; fen + oui = 'marsh yes'",
    "reading": "Affirmation of the bog — a yes spoken from the wet, fecund ground.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Fenway → 'wean fy' (old) → 'wean' (to detach) + 'fy' (fie, shame)",
    "reading": "To wean from the fen — a severing from the primal mire, a call to leave the swamp.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "F-E-N-W-A-Y → Fons, Emanatio, Numen, Via, Aeternitas, Yggdrasil",
    "reading": "Source, outflow, divine will, path, eternity, world-tree — the fen as cosmic axis.",
    "languages": ["la", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "F (fire) + E (earth) + N (water) + W (air) + A (spirit) + Y (the fork, choice)",
    "reading": "The five elements plus the forked path — a crossroads of all matter and spirit.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.35
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "F=6, E=5, N=14, W=23, A=1, Y=25 → sum = 74; 7+4=11; 1+1=2",
    "reading": "Seventy-four reduces to eleven, the master number of revelation, then to two — duality of land and water.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc"],
    "source": "generative (Pythagorean reduction)",
    "confidence": 0.45
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Fen + way; 'fen' (fr) = hay, but 'faim' = hunger; 'way' = voie; faim + voie = hungry road",
    "reading": "The road of hunger — a path that consumes those who walk it, a marsh that swallows.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.55
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Fenway < Old Norse fen (marsh) + vegr (way); cf. Icelandic fenvegur",
    "reading": "The Viking track through the bog — a Scandinavian loan-path in English soil.",
    "languages": ["en", "non"],
    "source": "Cleasby-Vigfusson, An Icelandic-English Dictionary, s.v. fen, vegr",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Fen (en) ~ 'fin' (fr) = end; way ~ 'oui' (fr) = yes; fin + oui = 'end yes'",
    "reading": "The final affirmation — a yes at the end of the path, a closing of the way.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Fenway → 'new fay' → fay (en) = fairy, elf; new fay = fresh spirit of the marsh",
    "reading": "A newborn fairy of the fen — the marsh's spirit reborn in a new form.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "F-E-N-W-A-Y → Fons, Emanatio, Numen, Via, Aeternitas, Yggdrasil (reversed: Yggdrasil, Aeternitas, Via, Numen, Emanatio, Fons)",
    "reading": "The world-tree reversed — the path from eternity back to the source, a circular return.",
    "languages": ["la", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  }
]
